bullets.title: FOMC Minutes Hawkish: Rate Hike Signaled If Inflation Stays Elevated
bullets.body: July FOMC minutes showed multiple participants favored a rate hike and 'many' said a hike would be 'likely needed' if inflation did not decline; three officials dissented hawkishly. Chair Warsh separately floated reducing scheduled meetings from 8 to 6 annually. Jan Hatzius (Goldman) forecasts core PCE slowing to 2.9% by December 2026, but 22V Research flags rising odds of hikes if nominal GDP stays at +5.7%. Hedgeye's August CPI nowcast was raised to +3.48% y/y.

bullets.title: Treasury Doubles Long-End Buybacks to $4B — Market Views Move as Temporary
bullets.body: Treasury unexpectedly doubled long-end buyback operations from $2bn to $4bn, effective Sept 9, driving 30-year yields down ~9-10bp and gold +3.5% to $4,500. JPM and Wolfe characterize the move as 'symptom relief, not root-cause fix' given the 6% budget deficit and $40 trillion national debt milestone hit Tuesday. Wolfe sees 10Y fair value at 4.4-4.5% with a 4.75% ceiling; durable yield relief requires softer growth data or BoJ normalization.

bullets.title: Rates + Debt: $40T National Debt, Structural Term Premium Rise, Private Investor Dominance
bullets.body: US national debt crossed $40 trillion Tuesday (+$60.8B in one day), with interest payments now $1.4T/year on track to surpass Social Security by 2028. Private investors now hold 73% of Treasury market vs. 50% a decade ago, and with hyperscaler capital competing for returns, yield premiums structurally must be higher. US debt/GDP is projected at 124% in 2026 versus 105% in 2016.

bullets.title: Sector Rotation: Healthcare vs. High-Beta Momentum Hits Historic Spread
bullets.body: XLV gained +3.5% in one of its best single days on record while the High Beta Momentum Basket collapsed -7.3% and Tech Systematic funds suffered their worst day since 2023 (>3 standard deviations). Software vs. Semis was +4.26% over two days and +9% over five. GS High Beta Momentum Pair is down ~13% over two sessions, and GS Broad AI basket and SPXXAI Index reached their most negative correlation on record. Piper Sandler recommends reducing semiconductor exposure or rotating to Software.

bullets.title: Pre-Market Tape: S&P Futures +0.48%, 10Y Yields Up 7bps to 4.70%, Oil +3.4%
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures are +0.48% to 7,691 heading into Thursday open, with 10-year yields up 7bps to 4.70%. Oil surged ~3.4% (WTI ~$88, Brent ~$93) on Iran escalation—Trump announced 'the most crushing economic operation ever' against Iran, froze negotiations, and threatened consequences for any country providing financial lifelines to Tehran. Bitcoin topped $70k on a short squeeze and Trump's Crypto Clarity Act push.

bullets.title: Iran Geopolitics Dominate: Strait of Hormuz, Oil, and 'Economic D-Day'
bullets.body: Trump froze Iran negotiations for weeks, vowed an 'Economic D-Day' against any nation supporting Tehran, and threatened intense military action if economic pressure fails. US forces quietly opened a Hormuz shipping corridor moving ~10M bpd (~50% of pre-war volumes), while diesel margins exceeded $100/bbl and US refinery runs hit their highest since 2019. The Iran-Oman talks reportedly broke down weeks ago.

bullets.title: AI Demand Signal Strengthening; Inflection Shifts to CY28 Not CY26/27
bullets.body: Wolfe, Jefferies, and JPM all note AI demand is strengthening, not weakening. Key data points: NVDA July quarter expected at $95B (vs $91.9B street) with a $108B October guide; MRVL Google deal implies $120B cumulative revenue through FY33; OAI locked in compute through 2030; and cloud revenue inflecting higher at MSFT and AMZN. The structural AI inflection is now pegged at CY28, driven by $500bn NVDA financing and AVGO's 20GW capex commitments.

bullets.title: 2Q26 S&P Earnings: 78% Beat Rate, Tech+ EPS +50.6%, TECH Broadening Expected
bullets.body: With 85.8% of S&P 500 market cap reported, 78% of companies beat estimates and earnings are topping projections by 7.3% in aggregate, with revenues up 15.5% and EPS up 33.4% YoY. TECH+ group leads at +50.6% EPS growth. Mag7 revenues and cash levels reduce valuation sensitivity to bond yields. JPM remains tactically bullish and expects broad-based re-levering from buybacks, retail, and systematic buyers.

bullets.title: Hedge Fund Positioning: De-grossing Continues, AI Winners Cut -0.8SD
bullets.body: Hedge funds reduced AI Winners and Hyperscaler exposure by -0.8 standard deviations each. Net leverage is near 12-month lows with US de-grossing at a -1.4z pace week-over-week. European funds are seeing a faster positioning rebound. Tech remains the most net-bought US sector in August, but net exposure in the Broad AI index remains well below May highs.

bullets.title: Global Manufacturing PMI Set to Cool; US to Outperform Foreign Markets
bullets.body: Global manufacturing is slowing as lagged easing cycle benefits fade and higher energy input prices bite. US ISM PMI is forecast at 54.3% in 2027 while the Eurozone PMI is expected at 50.8% and broader foreign PMI at 50.4%. Germany July PPI surged to 3.0% YoY (vs. 2.5% estimate and 1.8% prior), signaling persistent inflation pressure in Europe.

bullets.title: China Restricts Germanium and Quartz Exports to Taiwan; Semi Supply Chain Risk
bullets.body: China is stalling exports of germanium and quartz-based products to Taiwan, materials critical for optics and semiconductor manufacturing. Ajinomoto also cut ABF chip packaging film shipments to China by 30% following Beijing's rare earth export curbs, accelerating domestic Chinese substitution efforts.

bullets.title: Retail Spending Data Mixed; Consumer Stress Visible in DIY and Homegoods
bullets.body: KeyBanc proprietary card data shows all-retail spending growth decelerated to +1.7% for the week of Aug 16, below the 6-week avg of +2.1% and June's +4.5%. Citi CC data shows Homegoods spending down -2.1% YoY with transactions -3.2% YoY. AAP 2Q comp of -0.5% (vs +1.4% street) confirmed DIY household spending pressure, with the last 4 weeks especially weak.

bullets.title: WMT 2Q: EPS Beat but Comp Missed; Q3 Guide Light on Tariff Reinvestment
bullets.body: Walmart reported 2Q adj. EPS of $0.81 vs. guidance of $0.72-$0.74, but US SSS of +2.6% missed the +3.5% consensus. eCommerce grew 23% globally and advertising +38%. Q3 EPS guidance of $0.62-$0.64 missed the $0.68 consensus as the company is expected to reinvest tariff refund proceeds. Multiple analysts note the tariff refund masked core profitability weakness.

bullets.title: OpenAI ARR Surging ~250% YoY; IPO Targeted for 2027 or Sooner
bullets.body: OpenAI's Q2 revenue was +18% to $6.7B, with August ARR now at $40B implying ~250% YoY growth per GS TMT. Enterprise revenue run-rate is up 50% and AI coding/work products reached 20M weekly active users. OpenAI CFO told employees the company will go public in 2027 or sooner.

bullets.title: Russell 2000 Outperforming: +22.2% YTD vs S&P +12.6%; Earnings Tracking 2.8% Above Estimates
bullets.body: Russell 2000 was up 0.5% on Aug 19, outperforming the S&P 500 by 0.3%. YTD the small-cap index is up 22.2% versus the S&P's +12.6%. Russell 2000 earnings are tracking 1.2% above expectations (2.8% ex-financials) with revenues 3.5% above (4.0% ex-financials), suggesting broad fundamental support beneath the index.

bullets.title: Bitcoin Tops $70K on Short Squeeze and Trump Crypto Clarity Act Push
bullets.body: Bitcoin cleared its 200-day MA at $69k and bounced off its 200-week MA at $64k, surging above $70k on a short squeeze and Trump's public push for Congress to pass the Crypto Clarity Act. Crypto stocks rallied in pre-market with BTDR +5.8% on a Barclays overweight initiation. Treasury buybacks and dollar weakness (3-month low) further fueled the move.

bullets.title: Energy Sector: S&P Energy Up 40% YTD, Double Tech Gains; Oil at YTD Highs
bullets.body: The S&P Energy Sector is up 40% YTD 2026, double the tech sector's gains. WTI settled near $85.83/bbl (+1.05%) and Brent at $91.62/bbl (+0.66%), with intraday spikes driven by Iran escalation. US refinery runs hit the highest since 2019 while distillate stockpiles fell and diesel margins surpassed $100/bbl. Gulf tanker demand is surging to record charter rates.

bullets.title: Semis Fell Below 50-Day MA; AI vs Non-AI Correlation Hits Record Low
bullets.body: Semiconductor stocks fell below their 50-day moving average and are down ~16% from all-time highs. The GS Broad AI basket and SPXXAI index recorded their most negative correlation on record versus non-AI stocks. Retail flows into semis remain positive on fundamental conviction—semiconductor industry sales accelerated +134% YoY with ex-memory up 38% YoY.

bullets.title: BABA Q1: Revenue Slight Beat, EPS Miss; Cloud +45% YoY, Capex +75% YoY
bullets.body: Alibaba reported Q1 revenue of CNY268.95B (vs. CNY268.48B estimate) but EPS of CNY8.52 missed the CNY10.14 consensus. AI Cloud revenue accelerated to +45% YoY to CNY48.44B while capex surged 75% YoY to CNY67.68B vs. Tencent's CNY53bn, driving FCF deeply negative at -CNY44.67B. Operating margin compressed 8pp to 6% YoY.

bullets.title: Healthcare Sector: Negative Correlation to Tech for First Time in 5 Years; AI-Biotech Up 14% YTD
bullets.body: Healthcare is showing a negative correlation to technology for the first time in five years. Historically healthcare outperforms 60-90 days before/after midterm elections. AI-driven biotech firms (with 80-90% Phase I success rates) have outperformed the S&P 500 by 14% YTD, and life sciences baskets are the top-performing thematic strategy since June per Citigroup.
